metadata.scenario: A patient's wife calls saying they received a bill for a visit that was supposed to be covered by insurance. She says the office told her it would be fully covered when she scheduled. She wants the charge removed or an explanation of why insurance denied it.

transcription.text: Thank you for calling CareFirst Home Health, this is Margaret. How can I assist you today? Hi Margaret, this is Michael Brown. I'm calling regarding a bill we received for my father's care. I'm sorry to hear that, Michael. Can you please provide me with more details about the bill? Sure, we were told when we scheduled the visit that it would be covered fully by insurance, but we got charged anyway. I understand. That sounds frustrating. Can you tell me the date of the visit? It was last Tuesday, and it was for medication management and wound care. Thank you for that information. Let me pull up your father's account to check the billing details. Okay, I appreciate it. It just seems unfair, especially since we were assured it would be covered. I completely understand your concern, Michael. I’ll look into whether there was a coding error or if the insurance company denied the claim for some reason. Alright, I hope it’s just a misunderstanding. Yes, that’s likely. I’ll have to check the specifics. Can you hold for just a moment while I gather that information? Sure, take your time. Thank you for waiting. I see that the visit was coded under skilled nursing care, which can sometimes face coverage issues. So, is there a way we can appeal or get this resolved? Yes, we can certainly appeal the denial. I can help you with that process. It might also be helpful to confirm your insurance benefits with them. That sounds good. I want to make sure we don’t have to pay for this out of pocket. Understood. I can also assist with a follow-up visit for your father for continued care, which may help prevent issues going forward. Yes, that would be great. What kind of follow-up services do you provide? We offer skilled nursing care, medication management, and wound care. Those visits usually range from $95 to $125. That sounds reasonable. I'd like to get that scheduled, especially since his care is important. Absolutely, let’s set that up. In the meantime, let’s also ensure we get that billing issue resolved. Thank you, Margaret. What do I need to do next? I’ll initiate the insurance appeal today, and I’ll need your contact information for follow-up. Can I have your email? Yes, it’s mbrown@email.com. Perfect, Michael. I’ll send you an update on the appeal and the follow-up appointment details within 48 hours. That sounds great. Thank you for your help! You’re welcome! If you have any other questions, feel free to reach out. Will do. Have a great day! You too, Michael. Goodbye!
